title: jira-to-local configuration
description: Project settings for pulling Jira issues into a local folder. Holds no secret: the API token and email stay in the environment.

domain.description: Atlassian site host, without a scheme. Example: mycompany.atlassian.net

source.description: Where the credentials come from. Only the environment is supported, so the token is never written to this file.

key.description: Jira project key, uppercase. Example: PROJ

metaFields.description: Which of this site's custom fields fill the fixed metadata rows of content.md. Jira gives these a different customfield_NNNNN id on every site, so they cannot be hard-coded; setup detects them by display name. A role left unmapped is written as an em dash rather than guessed, and its field, if ticked, is still written as an ordinary field.

team.description: Field id for the Team row. Example: customfield_NNNNN

sprint.description: Field id for the Sprint row. On a scrum board this holds an array of sprint objects.

storyPoints.description: Field id for the Story Points row. Must hold a number.

roughStoryPoints.description: Field id for a second, coarser estimate row, where a project keeps one. Most do not — leave it out.

dueDate.description: Field id for a custom due date. Jira's own `duedate` is used first; this only fills the row when that is empty.

development.description: Field id for the development panel summary, which is split into the Git and Releases rows. Maintained by a source-control integration and read-only.

epicLink.description: Field id for the legacy Epic Link. Fills no row of its own — the Parent row supersedes it — but mapping it suppresses the field, so it is not written a second time.

checklistFields.description: The fields a Checklist app writes into, so content.md can rebuild them as one list of real checkboxes. Site-specific ids, like every custom field. Omit the block on a project with no checklist app and no section is written.

contentYaml.description: The YAML field. The only field carrying each item's checked state.

text.description: The rendered text field. Item names, no state.

boards.description: Optional. The boards the team actually uses, as ticked during setup. A project commonly has several; the pull does not read this, it is a note for a human.

type.description: scrum or kanban, as the agile API reports it.

instructions.description: Free text an agent reads before it fetches anything. Local conventions, which field really holds what, anything about this project the API does not say.

dir.description: Destination folder, relative to the workspace root. One subfolder per issue key is created inside it.

layout.description: Documentation only. The layout is always <dir>/<KEY>/.

maxMb.description: Attachments at or below this size are downloaded. Larger ones are listed with their size and the reason.

imagesOnly.description: When true, only image attachments are downloaded. Videos and PDFs are listed instead.

subdir.description: Folder inside the issue folder where linked pages are written.

maxDepth.description: 0 pulls the linked page alone. 1 adds its direct children, and so on.

issueTypes.description: Keyed by the Jira issue type name exactly as the API returns it. Stock names like Story, Task and Sub-task work, and so do the types a project invented for itself, whatever they are called — no code change either way.

docType.description: Short lowercase label for this type, used in reports.

instructions.description: Appended to the top-level instructions when this type is pulled.

fields.description: The fields to write first, in this order, each under its own heading. Only ticked fields are written; an unticked field is not reported.

name.description: The field's display name in Jira, for reports and for finding it again.

heading.description: The markdown heading written into content.md. Kept separate from name so a Jira rename does not move the headings.
